'''Estral Esports''' is a Latin American team founded in March 2019 by warehouse management system company [https://www.estral.com.mx/ ESTRAL].

== History ==

=== Early Years and LLA Ascension (2019–2023) ===
Estral Esports began its journey in May 2019 by acquiring the spot of the first champions from the [[Circuito Nacional México/2019 Season/Opening Season|Circuito Nacional México]], LanTV, after they got their promotion to the [[División de Honor]]. After achieving a "three-peat" as national champions and winning the [[Regional Norte 2020]], the organization joined the [[LLA|Liga Latinoamérica]] in 2021 by acquiring the spot of [[Pixel Esports Club]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tf-sSX6i8ms Detalles de la llegada de Estral a nuestra LLA (Spanish)] ''youtube.com''</ref> 

During their first three years in the LLA, Estral established itself as a premier contender, consistently reaching grand finals in the [[LLA/2021 Season/Closing Season|2021 Closing]], [[LLA/2022 Season/Opening Season|2022 Opening]], and [[LLA/2023 Season/Closing Season|2023 Closing]] splits. Despite multiple runner-up finishes, they fostered one of the largest fanbases in the region.

=== The Isurus Partnership and LTA Era (2024–2025) ===
After several years of contention, Estral finally claimed their first regional title during the [[LLA/2024 Season/Opening Season|2024 Opening Season]], defeating [[Movistar R7]] and representing Latin America at [[MSI 2024]].<ref>[https://lolesports.com/article/medallero-hist-rico-en-latinoam-rica/blt92678f1a0ecf8cf6 Medallero histórico en Latinoamérica (Spanish)] ''lolesports.com''</ref>

In late 2024, following the restructuring of the American competitive scene into the [[LTA|League of the Americas]], Estral Esports announced a strategic merger with the legendary Argentine organization, [[Isurus]]. Competing as '''[[Isurus Estral]]''' during the 2025 season, the partnership combined the historical legacy of both clubs. However, in June 2025, the organizations announced a mutual agreement to end the partnership. Isurus retained the slot in the [[LTA South]], while Estral Esports began looking toward a new international chapter.<ref>[https://x.com/EstralEsports__/status/1855036259036549609 Isurus and Estral Esports Partnership Announcement.] ''x.com''</ref>

=== Migration to Brazil and Tier 3 Run (2026–Present) ===
Following the split from Isurus, Estral Esports shifted its focus toward the Brazilian region. For the 2026 season, the organization actively sought a franchise spot in the newly independent [[CBLOL/2026 Season|CBLOL 2026]]. After failing to secure a direct slot in the top flight, the management decided to build a path from the ground up by entering the Brazilian Tier 3 scene.

Operating with a high-performance facility in Brazil, Estral competed in the [[Circuito Desafiante/2026 Season/Split 1 Qualifier|2026 Circuito Desafiante Open Qualifier]]. The team achieved a perfect run, winning every single match of the tournament without a loss. This undefeated performance secured their promotion to the [[Circuito Desafiante/2026 Season/Split 1|CD 2026]], where they currently compete with the goal of reaching the CBLOL through the promotion/relegation system.
